newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo June dept store sales fall 5.6 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo June dept store sales fall 5.6 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Sales at department stores in Tokyo declined 5.6 percent in June from a year earlier to 193.6 billion yen, the Japan Department Stores Association said on Tuesday.

Sales in Tokyo area department stores in the six months to June, meanwhile, fell 0.8 percent from the same period a year earlier to 1.17 trillion yen, the association said. The study covered 30 outlets of 14 department stores in the Tokyo area.

Business in June was slow as bad weather including two typhoons swept the nation, and sales fell in reaction to a rush in demand ahead of the rise in the consumption tax to five percent from three percent on April 1, the association said in a statement.
In general, buying by individual consumers remained at a low level, but corporate demand showed a slight recovery compared with May, it said.

Sales of furniture and household electrical appliances continued to be sluggish, declining 15.3 percent from a year earlier, while sales of clothing slipped 6.5 percent year-on-year, the association said.
Food and related products saw a slight recovery.

Unfavourable weather and the rise in the consumption tax prompted consumers to refrain from spending, but unusually high temperatures in July are raising hopes of higher sales among department stores, an analyst at Yamaichi Securities said.
